frames.narration: A database fails and 480 alerts arrive from 40 services in one minute. The engine groups them by service and dependency into a single incident, INC-52, and takes the worst severity: severity 1.
The engine asks the pager to page the primary on call. The page is a durable job with a five minute deadline, sent as a push notification, then SMS, then a voice call.
The primary does not answer. After five minutes the pager escalates to the secondary, who acknowledges within a minute. That ends the escalation, and the secondary becomes incident commander.

Because this is severity 1 the engine also pages a communications lead. Every step so far is appended to the timeline with a sequence number: the alerts, both pages, the missed acknowledgement and the two roles.
The communications lead writes one update: customers cannot check out, and the team is investigating. It is published to the static status page, and the same update goes to the fan-out queue.

The fan-out job splits the 200,000 subscribers into 400 batches of 500. Workers send each message with a key made of the update and the subscriber, so a retry cannot send a second copy. Failed sends are retried with backoff, and every message links back to the status page.

The update is recorded in the timeline with the delivery counts, so the postmortem can later say exactly when customers were told. The commander follows the runbook, rolls back the release, and the alerts resolve.

The postmortem is created from the timeline with the facts already filled in. Action items are given owners and due dates, and the status page shows the incident as resolved to everyone who had been told it started.
